lines.text: Two molecules can contain the same number of carbon atoms yet connect them in a chain, a side chain, or a ring. Tracing connectivity helps you recognise the carbon skeleton before discussing shape or reactions.

Describe an organic molecule as straight chained when its carbon atoms form one unbranched open chain, the chain may be drawn as a zigzag. Describe it as branched when a carbon side chain is attached to a main carbon chain. Describe it as cyclic when its atoms form a closed ring. Butane is straight chained, two methylpropane is branched, and cyclohexane is cyclic. These labels are about which atoms are joined, not the visual straightness of lines in a diagram.
Use the structural or skeletal formula you already know, follow every carbon end and vertex. You will then be able to separate connectivity from the three dimensional shape at each carbon.
Straight chained, one unbranched open carbon chain. Branched, a carbon side chain attached to the main chain. Cyclic, a closed ring of atoms. A zigzag drawing can still show a straight chain.
Why can a zigzag skeletal formula still represent a straight chained molecule?

Which feature makes a carbon skeleton branched? A bend in a drawn bond A side carbon chain attached to the main chain A double bond A closed ring B Branching is a connection in the carbon skeleton, bends in a drawing do not create branches.
The angles around carbon control how an organic molecule occupies space. A single molecule can contain different carbon shapes, so classify each atom locally.

Hybridisation is mixing of atomic orbitals on an atom to form orbitals used in sigma bonding. Four sigma bond directions at an s p cubed carbon produce a tetrahedral arrangement with bond angles about one hundred and nine point five degrees. Three sigma bond directions at an s p squared carbon produce a trigonal planar arrangement with angles about one hundred and twenty degrees and leave one unhybridised p orbital. Two sigma bond directions at an s p carbon produce a linear arrangement with a one hundred and eighty degrees angle and leave two unhybridised p orbitals. For example, ethane carbon is s p cubed, ethene carbon is s p squared, and ethyne carbon is s p. The listed angles are approximate when the attached groups differ.
The electron domain idea from VSEPR predicts the same local geometries. Hybridisation also tells you how many unhybridised p orbitals are available for pi bonding.

s p cubed, four sigma directions, tetrahedral, about one hundred and nine point five degrees. s p squared, three sigma directions, trigonal planar, about one hundred and twenty degrees. s p, two sigma directions, linear, one hundred and eighty degrees. Classify each atom from its own bonding.
Why is the methyl carbon in propene tetrahedral while the two alkene carbons are trigonal planar?

What is the local geometry of a carbon with three sigma bond directions and one unhybridised p orbital? Tetrahedral Trigonal planar Linear Square planar B Three s p squared orbitals form the trigonal planar sigma framework, the remaining p orbital can form a pi bond.
A bond line in a structural formula can hide more than one type of orbital overlap. Separating sigma and pi components lets you count bonds correctly.

A sigma bond forms by end on orbital overlap along the line joining two nuclei. A pi bond forms by sideways overlap of parallel unhybridised p orbitals above and below the sigma framework. An s p cubed atom uses its hybrid orbitals for sigma bonds and normally has no unhybridised p orbital for pi bonding. An s p squared atom uses three hybrid orbitals for sigma bonds and has one p orbital for one pi bond. An s p atom uses two hybrid orbitals for sigma bonds and has two p orbitals for two pi bonds. Thus a C C single bond contains one sigma, a C equals C double bond one sigma plus one pi, and a C is identical to C triple bond one sigma plus two pi bonds. C H sigma bonding can involve carbon hybrid orbital overlap with hydrogen one s.
The hybridisation and shapes you just classified explain the remaining p orbitals. When counting, first give each connected atom pair one sigma bond, then count extra pi bonds from multiple bonds.

sigma end on overlap along the internuclear axis. pi sideways overlap of unhybridised p orbitals. Single, one sigma, double, one sigma and one pi, triple, one sigma and two pi. s p squared leaves one p orbital, s p leaves two.
Why does a C equals C double bond contain one sigma bond and one pi bond rather than two sigma bonds?
How many pi bonds are in one C is identical to C triple bond? Zero One Two Three C One bond component is sigma and the other two are pi bonds from two pairs of p orbitals.
Organic structures are often printed flat, but their atoms may occupy three dimensional positions. The word planar is a claim about actual atom positions.

Planar means that the atoms being described lie in the same plane. In ethene, both carbon atoms are s p squared hybridised and trigonal planar. The carbon atoms and all four hydrogen atoms lie in one plane, so the whole ethene molecule is planar. The unhybridised p orbitals are perpendicular to this plane and overlap sideways to form the pi bond. Do not infer planarity solely from a flat drawing, cyclohexane has tetrahedral s p cubed carbon centres and normally adopts a non planar, puckered ring. A trigonal planar group within a larger molecule need not make every atom of that molecule coplanar.
Use local shapes from hybridisation to test planarity. This matters when interpreting molecular structures and distinguishing a planar alkene unit from a non planar saturated ring.

Planar, the atoms under discussion lie in the same plane. All six atoms of ethene are planar. A saturated cyclohexane ring normally puckers and is non planar. A flat paper diagram does not prove planarity.
Why does a flat hexagon drawing fail to show the actual three dimensional shape of cyclohexane?

In one breath.

Carbon connectivity tells you whether a molecule is straight chained, branched or cyclic. The bonding at each atom determines its local shape, bond angles, and the arrangement of sigma and pi bonds, a flat drawing alone cannot establish whether a molecule is planar.
Key ideas.

A straight chain molecule has an unbranched carbon chain, even when its structural formula is drawn as a zigzag. A branched molecule has a side carbon chain attached to the main chain. A cyclic molecule contains a closed ring of atoms. For example, butane is straight chained, two methylpropane is branched, and cyclohexane is cyclic. These words describe connectivity. A ring drawn as a hexagon on paper need not be flat in three dimensions.

Hybridisation describes the mixing of atomic orbitals on an atom to form orbitals used in its sigma bonding. Classify the atoms one at a time. An s p cubed carbon forms four sigma bond directions, giving tetrahedral local geometry and bond angles close to one hundred and nine point five degrees. An s p squared carbon forms three sigma bond directions in a trigonal planar arrangement, with angles close to one hundred and twenty degrees, one unhybridised p orbital remains. An s p carbon forms two sigma bond directions in a linear arrangement, with a one hundred and eighty degrees angle, two unhybridised p orbitals remain. These are approximate angles in molecules where substituents are not identical.

A sigma bond forms by end on overlap along the line joining two nuclei. A pi bond forms by sideways overlap of parallel unhybridised p orbitals, placing electron density above and below the sigma bond framework. A single bond contains one sigma bond. A double bond contains one sigma and one pi bond. A triple bond contains one sigma and two pi bonds. In ethane, each carbon is s p cubed and all C C and C H bonds are sigma. In ethene, each carbon is s p squared, the C equals C comprises one sigma and one pi bond. In ethyne, each carbon is s p, the C is identical to C comprises one sigma and two pi bonds. For C H sigma bonds, a carbon hybrid orbital overlaps end on with a hydrogen one s orbital.

Figure, Sigma bonds from end on overlap of s and p orbitals, source, nine seven zero one c13.3, p.7. Notice that each sigma bond, whichever orbitals formed it, ends up with its electron density symmetrical about the line joining the two nuclei.

Figure, Pi bonds from sideways overlap of p orbitals in s p squared and s p hybridised carbons, source, nine seven zero one c13.3, p.9. Notice that the p orbitals stay parallel and overlap sideways, so each pi bond is one bond with two lobes, one above and one below the sigma framework, the s p carbon pair carries two such pi bonds in perpendicular planes.

Planar means that the atoms under discussion lie in the same plane. All six atoms in ethene are planar, each carbon and its attached atoms have trigonal planar geometry, and the two carbon p orbitals overlap sideways. A saturated cyclohexane ring has tetrahedral s p cubed carbon centres and normally adopts a puckered, non planar conformation. Local trigonal planarity at one carbon does not guarantee that every atom of a larger molecule lies in one plane.

Figure, Ethene has two trigonal planar centres that share one plane, source, nine seven zero one c13.3, p.12. Notice that the two trigonal planar triangles drawn at the carbons lie in the same plane, which is why all six atoms of ethene, not just three at a time, are coplanar.
Method.
Trace the carbon skeleton and decide whether it is an open unbranched chain, an open branched chain, or a ring.
At each atom of interest, count sigma bond directions, four suggests s p cubed, three s p squared, and two s p. Name the corresponding local shape and approximate bond angle.
Count one sigma bond per connected pair of atoms. Add one pi for each double bond and two pi for each triple bond.
For a question about planarity, consider the positions of all specified atoms in three dimensions, especially around s p cubed centres.
Worked example.

In propene, C H three C H double bond C H two, the methyl carbon has four sigma bonds, so it is s p cubed, tetrahedral, and near one hundred and nine point five degrees. Each alkene carbon has three sigma bond directions, so it is s p squared, trigonal planar, and near one hundred and twenty degrees. The C equals C bond contains one sigma and one pi bond, its pi bond comes from sideways overlap of unhybridised p orbitals.
Traps.
Trap, Calling a zigzag chain branched. Why it's wrong, A bend on paper is not a side chain. Instead, Follow the carbon connections.
Trap, Counting a double bond as two sigma bonds. Why it's wrong, The second component is pi overlap. Instead, Count one sigma per connected pair, then add pi bonds.
Trap, Calling every ring planar. Why it's wrong, Saturated s p cubed ring atoms often pucker out of the drawing plane. Instead, Test the three dimensional geometry.
Exam technique.

For Describe, give the shape and angle together, tetrahedral one hundred and nine point five degrees, trigonal planar one hundred and twenty degrees, or linear one hundred and eighty degrees. For Explain, link the number of sigma bond directions and remaining p orbitals to the hybridisation and the resulting bonds. When a structure mixes single and multiple bonds, label each carbon separately before counting. In a bond counting answer, include the sigma component of every double or triple bond.
